title: Pressure-induced PT Symmetry Breaking in LaMnSi
authors: Takuya Aoyama, Hikaru Taneoka, Takemi Yamada, Hiroshi Tanida, Kenya Ohgushi
abstract: We investigate the magnetotransport properties of the antiferromagnetic metal LaMnSi, in which the collinear magnetic order breaks both spatial inversion (P) and time-reversal (T) symmetry yet preserves their combined PT symmetry. High pressure is found to suppress this PT-symmetric antiferromagnetic phase, inducing a transition into a PT-broken state characterized by a large anomalous Hall effect. Based on symmetry analysis, we propose a candidate magnetic structure for the high-pressure phase. Subsequent band calculations for this structure reveal the emergence of band splitting and orbital-dependent spin polarization. Our results establish LaMnSi as an ideal platform for controlling PT symmetry breaking via external parameters.
summary: This work explores how applying high pressure forces a quantum phase transition in LaMnSi, moving it from a PT-symmetric antiferromagnetic state to a PT-broken ferromagnetic state. This transition is experimentally marked by the emergence of a large anomalous Hall effect, which is theoretically linked to changes in spin polarization within the Mn $3d$ electronic bands.
main_problem: The study investigates how applying high pressure drives a quantum phase transition in the antiferromagnetic metal LaMnSi, specifically focusing on the breaking of combined PT symmetry.
main_result: High pressure suppresses the initial PT-symmetric AFM state, inducing a transition to a PT-broken FM state characterized by a large anomalous Hall effect (AHE).
method: The research combines electrical transport measurements (magnetotransport) under varying pressure and temperature with first-principles DFT calculations for electronic structure analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is the antiferromagnetic metal LaMnSi, which undergoes a structural/magnetic transition driven by external pressure. The analysis models the magnetic order using symmetry group theory ($	ext{B}_{1u}$ vs $	ext{A}_{2g}$) and electronic properties via DFT band structure calculations.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall Effect (AHE), magnetotransport coefficients ($ho_{yx}$, $\sigma_{xy}$), resistivity anomalies, and the magnetic ordering state (AFM to FM).
important_parameters: High pressure ($P \ge 5 	ext{ GPa}$), temperature ($T$), and the in-plane Mn–Mn interatomic distance.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that transport anomalies correlate directly with symmetry breaking, and DFT calculations are used to model the electronic consequences of proposed magnetic structures.
figures_summary: Figures show phase diagrams mapping $(	ext{PM}, 	ext{AFM}, 	ext{FM})$ regions based on $ho_{yx}$ vs $B$, alongside plots detailing temperature/pressure dependence of conductivity ($\sigma_{xx}$, $\sigma_{xy}$) and band structure asymmetry.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the ambient-pressure PT-symmetric AFM state via transport measurements, then demonstrating that increasing pressure drives a transition to a symmetry-broken FM phase evidenced by AHE. This is supported by theoretical DFT calculations confirming orbital-dependent spin polarization changes across the transition.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between external tuning (pressure) and fundamental symmetries ($	ext{PT}$ symmetry breaking) in determining electronic transport properties makes this highly relevant to understanding topological phases in condensed matter systems.

FIG. 4. Band structures (upper) and energy-dependent spin orbital occupancy of Mn 3d states below the Fermi level (lower) for LaMnSi. In the band structures, the up- and down- spin components of the Mn1 atom are represented by the sizes of the red and blue circles, respectively. Only the Mn1 atom is shown because the relations Mn2↑= Mn1↑and Mn2↓= Mn1↓hold in the FM state, whereas Mn2↑= Mn1↓and Mn2↓ = Mn1↑hold in the AFM state. Calculations assume the (a, c) AFM (B1u) and (b, d) FM (A2g) states.
